A British boy whose parents were once arrested for pulling him out of a hospital now appears to be free of cancer

This is kind of scary, because it's not like the parents were sending him to a 3rd world country to go through a dangerous un-proven therapy, but Photon Beam therapy, which (as I understand it) is nothing other than the next generation of traditional radiation therapy.

So, basically, the parents were arrested for wanting to have better machines zap their son's brain with radiation.

Having been close to friends and family within the US cancer treatment system - the US model is also alarming. Even in the best systems US medical care is an industrially applied model of healthcare for the most part now, and the effects of radiation treatment are terrible in the cancers I've seen. (Not a medical professional.) That a government would threaten prosecution of parents desperately seeking other treatment options is frightening, I very much agree.

Odd, because I don't find the US model "alarming". Maybe if you live in an area that does not have quality access to cancer treatment, you might believe so. The terrorifying part of this is not just that it's "other treatment options", the treatment that the parents wanted (and ultimately were able to get for their child) is an improvement on existing therapies, and very specifically of an even greater benefit to children, and still an even better treatment for cancers like brain cancer. Their kid was really the exact case that would achieve the greatest benefits from Proton Beam technology.

http://www.mayoclinic.org/proton-beam-therapy
My experience is at large US University-associated hospitals and medical centers and also some of the highest rated private hospitals in the US. The level of disorganization and errors was alarming.

I know people that avoid large university associated hospitals, research hospitals, or the 'go to place' for that very reason. Again, I must be lucky to have a handful of topnotch places around me. Or, unlucky enough to be living in an area where the current population is paying for the mistakes of the past.

Live and learn, in this too. Best to accept that death is coming for us all, not expect miracles, or even that, say, medical staff and facilities could keep track of one's medication allergies. = o One lesson learned is that patients need advocates to go with them to appts, for treatments, and to just be an "extra set of ears". There's a tremendous amount of information to be kept track of on all sides and having that extra person or two who helps out is critical. Medical mistakes are rampant because of these issues, in part. I could go look something up and post a link but know you can do that yourself if you are not already aware of this issue. :-) Time for lunch!

Enjoy the lunch. Something that I hold near and dear to me is (and this goes for anyone reading this really) don't be afraid to look to see what groups are out there locally and nationally that can help. Even simple things like checking out your local Relay for Life events might be just the pick-me-up that someone needs to put smile on their face, if only for a few brief moments.

I'm only confused as to what the parents were going to get charged with, as I didn't see that specifically mentioned in the article. Is it a crime to defy doctors orders in the UK? I know the US is much different, in that, a child can have their parents say no to, for example, a blood transfusion if they're Jehovah's witnesses (which is disallowed in that religion).

Anyone have any more info or sources?
This authoritarian level of control definitely seems to be rearing its ugly head in our world way too often, I hope it works out well for the parents, they did the right thing in this situation
